findings.explanation: SPL alerts on more than 10 addresses per day, the description lists >20/>10/>5/>1 as alert conditions, and detailedImplementation alerts at >20 with a CRITICAL level at >50; meanwhile the data-source text says iOS/Android normally use 8-12 addresses per day, so a >10 trigger will fire on ordinary phones.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one alert threshold, raise it above the documented normal for mobile devices (or segment by device type), and use the same churn bands in SPL and prose.

findings.explanation: Verified status with a group reviewer, while the numeric baselines (3-5 addresses on desktops, 8-12 on phones) are unsourced and the thresholds are inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark as draft until baselines are measured on the local network.

findings.explanation: The per-OS address counts are given without a source and may not reflect RFC 8981 defaults (preferred lifetime one day) for these platforms; the Windows/macOS figures are also unsourced.
findings.quote: iOS/Android: temporary addresses enabled, very aggressive churn (~8-12 addresses/day) to defeat WiFi tracking.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite vendor documentation or measure on your own clients before publishing numeric baselines.

findings.explanation: A device may have several link-local addresses and many systems use stable-privacy or random interface identifiers rather than MAC-derived ones, so the reasoning for filtering fe80:: is overstated.
findings.quote: every device always has exactly one link-local address derived from its MAC
findings.suggested_fix: Say link-local addresses are excluded because they do not rotate like temporary global addresses.

findings.explanation: Scenarios are template text; real causes such as container hosts, hypervisors and VPN or NAT64 gateways with many addresses per MAC, or routers that appear in the cache for many hosts, are only in troubleshooting.
findings.quote: Scheduled automation elevates `host` without crossing `addr_count` > 20 for UC-5.20.12.
findings.suggested_fix: Move those causes into knownFalsePositives and suppress by MAC.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Security and Compliance are listed for an address-hygiene metric whose compliance relevance is not stated; verify the intended mapping.

summary: A thoughtful use of NDP-cache data to measure temporary-address churn, but the alert thresholds conflict across SPL, description and prose, and the SPL's alert level would flag normal mobile devices. Template boilerplate remains in value, false positives and status.
